items.title: Slovenia becomes the sixth EU country with national customer approval
items.summary: Tesla Europe says Slovenia recognised the Dutch Article 39 file. Rollout expected soon. Six countries still cover only about 9.4% of the EU population.
items.why_it_matters: Still far from the TCMV thresholds (15 of 27 states and 65% of population).

items.title: France starts UTAC road tests after Musk–Tabarot FSD talks
items.summary: French Transport Minister Philippe Tabarot said he had a constructive exchange with Elon Musk on 2 September. Tesla provided two FSD Supervised series cars for independent UTAC on-road tests so France can verify Dutch/Tesla data on French roads before a possible TCMV vote (October rumour or early December). Reuters and Connexion France report the tests; this is not a French customer approval.
items.why_it_matters: France is a large-population swing vote for the 15-state / 65% TCMV bar. Testing after the July safety veto is a material thaw — still not an approval, and speed/attention concerns remain on the record.

items.title: Sweden restates ambition for Union-wide FSD Supervised approval
items.summary: In a written Riksdag answer dated 31 August 2026 (published 1 September), Infrastructure Minister Andreas Carlson said the government’s starting point and ambition is that a Union-wide approval of systems such as Tesla FSD (Supervised) should be put in place, after evaluations that include Trafikverket’s assessments. He did not lock in a yes vote and did not cancel Trafikverket’s speed-limit concerns.
items.why_it_matters: Official Swedish signal ahead of TCMV: Stockholm wants EU-wide clearance if the safety case holds, even while the agency has urged a no unless deliberate over-speed is removed.

items.title: Swedish transport minister filmed riding Tesla with FSD in Mullsjö
items.summary: Around 30 August 2026, Infrastructure Minister Andreas Carlson posted an Instagram Story of himself riding in a Tesla with FSD Supervised during authorised testing in Mullsjö (one of the Swedish municipalities with Transportstyrelsen test permits). The clip circulated on X via accounts such as @AlexanderKr; treat X amplification as rumour/secondary. ITavisen and local SVT coverage document the Mullsjö testing context. Not a national customer approval.
items.why_it_matters: Political visibility for supervised FSD in Sweden while TCMV talks continue — symbolic, not a regulatory green light for Swedish owners.

items.title: Norwegian Public Roads Administration page last updated 3 July 2026
items.summary: SVV restates: Norway is not customer-approved; limited testing only; customer demos blocked until Tesla changes messaging; next TCMV window in October.
items.why_it_matters: Official Norwegian baseline until SVV publishes a newer update.

items.title: TCMV discusses the Dutch Article 39 file — no vote
items.summary: Committee discussion on 30 June 2026 without a ballot. Norway participated without voting rights.
items.why_it_matters: First realistic vote window shifts toward autumn (October rumour: 6 Oct).
